title: Adaptive-horizon batcher: workload characterization, safety fences, and continuous rollout
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build an adaptive-horizon batching recommender that profiles per-customer and per-route workload distributions, computes safe continuous-batching parameters (target batch sizes, max-await, decay windows), and provides a canary/rollback flow for automatic application. Focus is on minimizing token-cost while keeping p99 tail latency SLOs and per-tenant SLAs intact.
acceptance_criteria: Recommender computes stable batch parameter sets for 90% of profiled routes without manual tuning
Canary rollout applies config to 5% traffic and automatically rolls back on defined latency/cost regressions within 30 minutes
Dry-run simulator predicts cost delta within ±8% vs real traffic for 72-hour validation windows
Telemetry shows no customer-visible p99 latency regressions when applied to Dedicated pools with sample load
solution_sketch: Offline profiler samples request traces (sequence length, model variant, prompt prefix entropy, arrival inter-arrival times) for rolling 7-day windows
Generate candidate batching configs using three heuristics: throughput-maximizing, tail-preserving, and cost-saving constrained by per-route latency budgets
Continuous controller exposes a horizon parameter (decay window) that interpolates between aggressive and conservative batching; tuned per-customer using historical tail-latency targets
Simulate dry-run by replaying sampled traces through a lightweight runtime model (KV cache hit modelling + batching latency estimator) to compute expected cost/latency impact
Safe apply flow: canary -> ramp -> automatic rollback with checkers (p99 latency, error rate, cold-start rate, cost spike) and manual override
Integrate with Console rollout UI and runtime-1.22 config APIs for observed/target metrics and audit logging
milestones: M1: Profiler prototype (3 days) - collect feature vectors and histogram outputs
M2: Heuristics engine (7 days) - implement three heuristics and scoring function
M3: Simulator & dry-run harness (6 days) - replay and cost/latency estimator
M4: Canary/rollback plumbing (4 days) - runtime toggles, alerting hooks
M5: Console integration + docs (3 days) - rollout UI and runbook
M6: Production experiment (2 weeks) - 5% canary ramp and validate
risks: Profiler sampling bias for low-volume tenants could recommend overly aggressive batching leading to tail regressions
Simulator model mismatch (KV cache effects under-estimated) could underpredict latency impacts
Cross-route packing interactions when multiple tenant configs are applied to same Dedicated pool
Automated rollback thresholds could be noisy during unrelated infra incidents and cause oscillation
mitigations: Add minimum-sample thresholds and fallback conservative presets for low-volume tenants
Calibrate simulator using A/B trials and backtest against historical incidents
Add global coordination layer to avoid conflicting batch policies within a GPU pool
Use smoothed metrics and hold windows for rollback triggers; add manual confirmation step for high-impact routes
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff — scope agreed with PM team (Claire Zhang). Selected features to collect: seq_len, tokens_added, arrival_delta, model_variant, prefix_similarity.
2026-03-04: Profiler stub committed — https://github.com/redwood-inference/profiler/pull/187 — initial histogram outputs validated on 48h sample of hosted traffic.
2026-03-06: Heuristics design reviewed with runtime team. Decided to use latency-weighted scoring instead of strict p99 clamp to avoid overfitting to spikes.
2026-03-08: Simulator prototype outputs compared to baseline for two routes — cost delta prediction within 12% initially; will iteratively tighten with calibration.
2026-03-10: Safety fences drafted — rollback checks will include p99 latency, p95 latency, error-rate, and cost-per-1000-token delta. Thresholds are configurable per-tenant.
2026-03-12: Canary plan approved by SRE and Product. Mateo to own canary runbook; DevEx to prepare Console toggles. Estimated production experiment start: 2026-03-25.
